| | Friend, I’m Taylor Pansing Brooks — Patty’s son and a proud LGBTQ+ Nebraskan. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/49382187/361917459/333259033?amount=25&refcode=em_220817_fromtaylor_rs2&sourceid=1030989&ms=em_220817_fromtaylor_rs2&refcode2=5fd6a2b4-881e-ed11-bd6e-281878b83d8a&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTMvMS85MzkxMCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI1ZmQ2YTJiNC04ODFlLWVkMTEtYmQ2ZS0yODE4NzhiODNkOGEiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=nUm-POg0mL-_80PPQpnCYEVQRuQ1Lt7Fr0-0sB-LzTQ=) I wanted to reach out because frankly, it’s **unconscionable** that our legislators continue to vote against what _should_ be our most fundamental human right: _The right to love whomever we love._ Nebraska hasn’t always been kind to our LGBTQ+ neighbors, and I’m grateful every day that I grew up in a family that has loved and accepted me every moment of every day, without reservation. Over the last eight years, my mom has fought fiercely on the floor of the Nebraska Legislature for people like me to live and love without fear of discrimination — at work, in our communities, and in the privacy of our homes. She knows that being gay, or bi, or trans, or gender nonconforming, isn’t a _choice_ — **it’s simply who we are.** The _choice_ lies in whether we come out as our true and authentic selves, or if we continue to suppress the most inextricable parts of our identity because it makes some of our elected officials uncomfortable. **People like Mike Flood are voting to keep us in the shadows. I say it’s time to rise up and vote him out of office this November.** | [VOTE FLOOD OUT THIS NOVEMBER »](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/49382189/361917462/333259033?amount=25&refcode=em_220817_fromtaylor_rs2&sourceid=1030989&ms=em_220817_fromtaylor_rs2&refcode2=5fd6a2b4-881e-ed11-bd6e-281878b83d8a&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTMvMS85MzkxMCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI1ZmQ2YTJiNC04ODFlLWVkMTEtYmQ2ZS0yODE4NzhiODNkOGEiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=nUm-POg0mL-_80PPQpnCYEVQRuQ1Lt7Fr0-0sB-LzTQ=)

Over the last eight years, my mom has fought fiercely on the floor of the Nebraska Legislature for people like me to live and love without fear of discrimination — at work, in our communities, and in the privacy of our homes. Hello,
As a naval officer, my husband’s absence was a frequent expectation. The longest deployment was 13 months, another was around 10 months. These absences were expected for me as his spouse. I knew when I met him that he was committed to serve this nation to the best of his ability.
Those long deployments were less understandable for our children. For a ten-year-old, dad being gone from one summer to the next constituted a really long time – the first set of braces, Dad’s Day at school, a family’s worth of holidays, birthdays, and anniversaries...missing him in the photos.
It was always a joyous occasion when he returned from deployment. Often we’d want to surprise the kids, which led to a trove of heartfelt memories, some really precious. Once when Michael got home in the middle of the night, our toddler daughter exclaimed, “Mommy! Who is that sleeping in your bedroom?” For a toddler, 8 months is a near-lifetime.
I have no regrets being a military spouse, because our life was full of adventure to keep it fun, adversity to make us strong, and an acknowledgement that duty was served. Michael never complained, although I could see in his eyes how much he regretted the lost years that pictures will never fully capture. He tears up over not having been home to see either child take their first step.
Michael is now the Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate against Chuck Grassley in Iowa. In taking this challenge on, he knows the commitment it’ll entail. But a commitment to service is what’s necessary for him to feel complete, to be the person he is. You see, he isn’t doing this because he wants to endure a nasty political campaign... he is running because he sees a duty to his fellow Iowans and this nation. He sees working in the Senate as a continuation of his many decades of service. Speak with him and you will quickly understand what drives him, where his heart is, and how well he relates with those struggling to make ends meet. In short, he gets it.
Of course, Chuck Grassley, Mitch McConnell, and their Super PACs are already starting to tell ridiculous, laughable lies about my husband. In one ad, they labeled Michael, a retired Vice Admiral, a radical socialist. Really? Good luck with that!
Michael doesn’t come from a political dynasty. No one in his family has ever been in politics. Like him, they are regular people, gifted with incredible work ethic and grounded in Iowa values.

body:
| | | |
---
| FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE THURSDAY, AUGUST 18
CITIZENS FOR A GREATER GEORGIA ANNOUNCES OVER 200,000 VOTER CONTACTS IN FIRST 90 DAYS ATLANTA - Today, Citizens for a Greater Georgia announced that it has made over 200,000 voter contacts since launching its statewide field program in June. The program, which is currently anchored by two-dozen paid field operatives, is dedicated to mobilizing disenfranchised, disengaged, and newly registered voters in key State Senate districts across the state. With a [target list](https://r20.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001gt_87esdGK_heVRM-exVkH6So835JXz7r6MFbGR4zxtzO21OGemr-IMhmd5U5Fcjwz-YYqC82wuuXszXP0nOKwYvBglS7grneO0IWJGU2jENmd5ZEAZc6ihXHhRNRE-pBTFluvWW-06t5PRO_3T0FBiXY4Z-6b106FVfJshnqrh8SToIQcjuHseZN_Wk9awT9bV25QFFOguJdgaZaoxIgzg7PZa7Iht15xYJ0rS9uFzvC9m6YAA-Hfc-m3Hvz08uVGZ-geHWPPRoRRUD0yzNcTs1ruLWO0L0yoCMqEbLllVOSFVJrBIWER9pGkzf0nLu&c=mcBBT_ih-xlhklCRPl2FOT6fA3-i23spS27e1CXCQxYkMhOSpLYXLQ==&ch=mjvS5QR4IVWZetWmDSNkYp9xUol7k4o58GJMvHKtpZJT1PqT7-p2OQ==) of candidates, Citizens is emphasizing several key hold and pickup opportunities across Cherokee, Cobb, Forsyth, Fulton, and Gwinnett Counties. To join our growing team, and to view paid positions, click [here](https://r20.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001gt_87esdGK_heVRM-exVkH6So835JXz7r6MFbGR4zxtzO21OGemr-I2VyfdPl_-ImXx03YN1WHDczVtRa9b8MsY8eQhp5mS4jJTWh7z1yhqSvrdQYPMNS-0hX5C-p5chd7k5fUJKbO1IqKHrD7ls8adXeo4A6gTbSOpU-sDl5Xc=&c=mcBBT_ih-xlhklCRPl2FOT6fA3-i23spS27e1CXCQxYkMhOSpLYXLQ==&ch=mjvS5QR4IVWZetWmDSNkYp9xUol7k4o58GJMvHKtpZJT1PqT7-p2OQ==). Results that the Citizens for a Greater Georgia team has delivered include:
* Over 200,000 voter contacts comprising:
* 46,522 voters reached at the doors
* 156,165 voters reached at the phones
* 14 Days of Action for canvassing and phone banking
* 13 community events with Republican groups, candidates, and campaigns
* Dozens of new volunteer recruits

"In just a few months, the Citizens for a Greater Georgia team has built, from the ground-up, a robust field operation that is working every day to preserve and grow our Republican State Senate Majority and keep our state strong," said State Senate Majority Caucus Chairman John F. Kennedy. "Throughout the summer, we have reached hundreds of thousands of voters - and as we enter into the final 80 days of the 2022 election cycle, we are expanding our team across the state - working on behalf of our State Senators, and Republicans up and down the ballot. I am deeply proud of the effort our team has put in on the ground so far - and look forward to delivering the results of this hard work come November."

https://www.catherineforcongress.com [https://www.catherineforcongress.com]
A champion to fight climate change
We are on the verge of a major point in the fight to combat climate change. It will take courage, dedication and leadership, but fortunately, there are leaders who know how to get the job done. They have a record of results when it matters most, and they are ready to get to work for us.
Unfortunately, our current Congressman doesn’t share that same priority.
There’s no denying that CATHERINE PARKER [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/catherineforcongress?refcode=activis] has the strongest record on combating climate change and funding flood mitigation in this race.
She’s worked for years to improve flood mitigation and enhance our infrastructure:
AUTHORED the unanimously passed Flood History Disclosure Law
RELAUNCHED the Long Island Sound Watershed Intermunicipal Council to help communities work collaboratively to mitigate flooding
ADVOCATED for funding for the Army Corp of Engineers project in Mamaroneck
ADDED over $11M dollars to flood mitigation projects in the county budget
FACILITATED the collaboration between Purchase College, Rye Brook and Rye to work together on Blind Brook flood mitigation
She’s fought climate change and strengthened conservation efforts right here in the district:
HELPED CREATE the County Office of Sustainability and the position of County Energy Director
CREATED a ban on dirty residual home heating oil and toxic plastics
PASSED ban on “Styrofoam” products
SPONSORED the Green Fleet Policy which transforms the county fleet from gas to electric
If you’re ready to take on climate with a champion for our environment, then Catherine Parker needs your vote on August 23rd.

| Hi Friends,
It's another exciting day on the campaign trail. Here are five things we want you to know about Geoff and Leah's campaigns today:

| 1\. Geoff Rejects Globe Editorial Board Meeting
---
| Yesterday, Geoff issued a public rejection of an invitation from the Boston Globe's editorial board to "interview" for the newspaper's endorsement. "I'm not going to waste time participating in a charade with one of the most liberal newspapers in the nation," Geoff said. | 2\. Ballot Question Petition Needs Your Signature!
---
| Thank you to all of the Diehl-Allen volunteers who have been out collecting signatures for the ballot question to repeal giving driver's licenses to illegal immigrants. If you haven't yet signed the petition, act fast - there are just a few days left to sign!
WRKO's Jeff Kuhner has a new column out that explains what's at stake, saying there's a possible "red wave" coming to Mass this fall. He also mentions how Geoff and Leah's campaigns have been instrumental in collecting signatures:
"Republican gubernatorial candidate, Geoff Diehl, is helping to spearhead the collection drive. Diehl is a Trump conservative, who believes in secure borders, election integrity and opposes illegal immigration.... This is the issue that can propel a stunning Republican upset and put a conservative populist in the governor's office."
---
| | [Read Jeff Kuhner's Latest Column](https://r20.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001rIZzW5bzpDmdYAti2em09EXeF3co0fCppHRzepNp5ZMiOm7ZxYfq7XVFSJujBsByZFsBSPtHw-cL6xxbg7exln1gCGJv_5I4OxYtg3JLOO7KvIY7v0rWSTgKmodi2_GpoD-i9hkQFomw9JISE7SykuaSPwXGUAEuxoebeeq5tyHvdOwz4OYDHY9fw1YmAYWv4KQ58yQbDIeDZNtBToPFB2Y-_4KvSFT2QrW5bWSggWfIz4L9-4cAZSrgd1o_XSg_&c=1QXEbwW4bDVIibzohEDDiuOEKbAxdpy2ItXTUi9F0DCgoIYZIloP9Q==&ch=Tqdh3ogvZQtZ2ZW1ZC8N2N6b55b3APqhmggtyZ7Go5apUpHYRYOLAg==)

| 3\. Joe Malone Endorses Geoff
---
| Geoff is proud to be endorsed by former Massachusetts State Treasurer Joe Malone and his wife, Linda Malone!

| 4\. MBTA Orange Line Closes Tomorrow
---
| The impending shutdown of the MBTA's Orange Line has everyone talking about how to address infrastructure. It's nice that other campaigns are finally catching up; Geoff's been talking about this issue for months! Check out the video below for some of his recent thoughts on the topic:
---

| Geoff had a great time out on the campaign trail in Western Massachusetts yesterday. One of his stops was at City Jake's Cafe in Springfield. Voters were very enthusiastic. There is a lot of interest in our campaign all across the state!

The lives of women and girls aren’t a joke. The anti-choice laws Charlie Crist championed for decades aren’t something that can be laughed off or swept under the rug.

subject: You helped us get this far, can we count on you one more time?

body:
Peter,

We wanted to take a moment to thank everyone who donated towards our mid-month fundraising goal – we couldn’t do it without you!

But, we did fall a little short, so we’re extending our mid-month fundraising deadline until midnight tonight to ensure we reach our $20,000 goal.

And today, we also celebrate the anniversary of the 19th Amendment, granting women the right to vote. The stakes for women couldn’t be more clear this year as the Supreme Court and state after state take aim at our reproductive freedom.

That’s why it’s critical we hit this goal, so we’re able to fund our voter outreach programs and reach every voter in the district – and that takes some serious funds.

We still need to raise $1,333. If everyone reading this donates even $1, we’d reach our $20,000 goal. Can you pitch in? Please donate today. https://secure.actblue.com/donate/lm-mm-aug22

Thank you,
Team Mathis

Peter,
Today, thanks to your hard work, we did it!

Wyoming has spoken on behalf of everyone all across this great country who believes in the American dream, who believes in liberty, and who recognizes that our natural rights -the freedom of speech, freedom of religion, equal protection and due process, come from God, they do not come from the Government.

And what Wyoming has shown today is that while it may not be easy, we can dislodge entrenched politicians who believe they've risen above the people they're supposed to represent.

By our vote today, Wyoming has put the elites on notice - we are no longer going to tolerate representatives who don't represent us.
---

Wyoming has drawn a line in the sand that if WE put you in power, you WILL be accountable to us, you WILL answer to us, and you WILL do what is in OUR best interest.

_And if you don't?
_
**We will fire you.

subject: Sign & send the petition to the National Academy of Medicine: The healthcare sector must divest from fossil fuels
body:
Add your name to support fossil fuel divestment
| | | | |
---
| | |
---
| | |
---
| | |
---
| |
---
| | | | | Peter, In response to the growing climate crisis, the National Academy of Medicine [has called on](https://default.salsalabs.org/Tce8ae2f3-5645-489c-a08b-fe8d5f3ee8ed/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9) health sector institutions to take greater responsibility for reducing greenhouse gas emissions – calling it the core of the crisis. That’s all well and good, except it does not address one of the root causes of the crisis at the source: the BILLIONS of dollars continuing to be invested into fossil fuel holdings by the health sector’s large private institutions’ pension and retirement funds. The urgency of the climate crisis, the implications for global public health and equity, and the health sector’s singularly unique responsibilities towards our health demands a response from the health sector that directly addresses this root cause. [**In order to address this blatant contradiction and confront the major health impacts caused by climate change, we are demanding the National Academy of Medicine call upon healthcare institutions to divest from fossil fuels.**](https://default.salsalabs.org/T00ee110d-55c6-440f-9cae-c1e014fffa28/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9)
---
| | [ADD YOUR NAME](https://default.salsalabs.org/T98b2ff2b-a689-4a75-a788-ede90a72a471/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9)
---
|
---
| | | Pension funds, globally, have hundreds of billions invested, in fossil fuel holdings. These investments provide the funding to develop massive fossil fuel infrastructure. Today, over 1,400 institutions have fossil fuel divestment [policies](https://default.salsalabs.org/T09c99636-013a-4b9e-b966-37e07a9beabf/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9) in place – **yet,** **not a single major U.S. healthcare institution is among them.** There are some 1,200 private hospital systems in the U.S., each with varying amounts of funds invested in oil, coal, or gas holdings. It’s absurd, and entirely hypocritical, for healthcare institutions to continue to make these investment choices. Hospitals divested from tobacco in the ‘90s, and they can – and must – divest from fossil fuels today. [**Sign and send the petition: Demand the the National Academy of Medicine issue a public statement supporting fossil fuel divestment in the healthcare sector.**](https://default.salsalabs.org/T9f926010-a031-4cc0-be39-7ed9b38a3975/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9)

name: Laurie Teper
subject: Thank You!
body:
Hello Team Geels!
Thank you to all who have stepped up and helped in some way. You are appreciated and valued! Courtney cannot win without engaged volunteers. This is a last reminder for the Person County Fundraiser happening tomorrow night! If you haven't already done so, please consider purchasing tickets and attending. You don't have to live in Person County to attend! Think of people who live in surrounding counties and make a phone call or shoot a text. You never know who might not know about this. If they trust you, they will trust Courtney. LAST CHANCE TO PURCHASE TICKETS since it's in a restaurant and they need a headcount.

Friday, August 19, 6pm-8pm
Homestead Steakhouse
205 Frank Timberlake Rd in Timberlake
Cost: $75
<https://courtneygeelsforcongress.com/event/courtney-geels-steakhouse-dinner/>

_Door Knocking in Durham_
Saturday, August 20, 9:00am-12:30pm
Meeting Place: Parking Lot at Northgate Mall near the C & H Cafeteria and where Sears (Guess Road) used to be.
Email Renee at [rhill632@gmail.com](mailto:rhill632@gmail.com) to get signed up!

_School Supplies Backpack Drive -__You don 't have to be there the entire time. Stop by for an hour or so!_
I'm happy to report that we fulfilled all the backpack needs! They upped the backpack count from 50 to 74 but between our volunteers and First Baptist Church volunteers, we came pretty close to getting everything. The fire department will hand them out Saturday.

Thank you for the supplies and willingness to help out at the event! There is a parking lot located by the community garden. Our role will be to have FUN hanging out with the kids and help the church's volunteers with crafts and pizza. Of course, if you get into any conversations with the parents, give your best plug for Courtney! Please wear your Courtney Geels shirts! This is an opportunity to be present and serve this community.

Saturday, August 20 1:00pm-4:00pm

642 S. Mebane St., Burlington

Fire, Police, Crafts, Pizza, Face Painting
Saturday, August 20 1:00pm-4:00pm

642 S. Mebane St., Burlington

Fire, Police, Crafts, Pizza, Face Painting - COME JOIN US AND HANG OUT WITH THE KIDS!

_Kinfolk Concert Series - Courtney has a booth_
Wear your shirt, stop by and say hi and enjoy the music!
Saturday, August 20, 7:00pm-9:00pm
Graham Amphitheater
104 East Elm St in Graham
Live Music
<https://www.visitalamance.com/event/kinfolk-concert-series%3A-side-kix/23716/>

**We are still looking for volunteers who will call people on a list that mailers were supposed to go to. Some people said they didn 't receive one or it got thrown out. It's also an opportunity to end the message with "I hope we can count on your vote for Courtney on November 8"! ** _Email your county coordinator or me if interested._

That's it for now! Have a fantastic weekend everyone!!

__Fighting for Truth, Justice and Unity Together!__
Laurie Teper
Volunteer Director
Courtney Geels for Congress NC04
Email: [volunteers@courtneygeelsforcongress.com](mailto:volunteers@courtneygeelsforcongress.com)
Cell: (847)212-5651
[courtneygeelsforcongress.com](http://courtneygeelsforcongress.com)

They’ve tried, over and over again, to defund the program so that hard-working young people won’t have access to the same retirement security and dignity that people my mother’s age have been able to rely on: [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/49386587/361958146/1023722261?refcode=protectsocialsecurity&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MjAzMyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzNDQ3ZGNjMi1mNDFlLWVkMTEtYmQ2ZS0yODE4NzhiODNkOGEiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=sMtFexOVNbA-Va_NwVviHylnFgaQEmXUPqNauaO8tsk=) **_ALL people deserve to live with dignity. Wisconsin has always been my home. I grew up on my family’s dairy farm in northern La Crosse County, among the rolling hills, coulees, and valleys of “God’s Country.”
As a farm boy, I learned the value of hard work, resilience, appreciation for the land, and respect for our community. The tried-and-true Wisconsin values my parents, neighbors, and teachers instilled remain with me today.
**Community service is one of those homegrown values and has informed my professional life.**
I earned my Bachelor of Arts degree in public and environmental administration from the University of Wisconsin — Green Bay and a Master of Public Administration from George Mason University.
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/49415224/362048791/404025521?refcode=E17852-20220818-BradStory-graphic-CampaignNews-RegTemplate-NA-NA&amount=25&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzEvMS85MzIyMyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3MzQ3ZjFhMi0xOTFmLWVkMTEtYmQ2ZS0yODE4NzhiODNkOGEiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=hmx5c-769MoWrCzgixDei-cYiLm0v9PwbEKhAF1tXpo=) _This is me and Betty who would go on to be my wife!_ In 1997, I joined the congressional staff of Rep. Ron Kind, assisting him with agriculture and rural development issues for over 12 years. I’ve also been honored to work for Senator Herb Kohl and state Rep. Virgil Roberts. Deciding it was time to get into the arena, in 2007, I was elected to the La Cross County Board of Supervisors. In 2009, friend, I was privileged to serve the Obama Administration as the Wisconsin executive director for the Farm Service Agency at the U.S. Department of Agriculture and then, in 2015, as the USDA Deputy Administrator for Farm Programs. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/49415225/362048792/404025521?refcode=E17852-20220818-BradStory-graphic-CampaignNews-RegTemplate-NA-NA&amount=25&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzEvMS85MzIyMyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3MzQ3ZjFhMi0xOTFmLWVkMTEtYmQ2ZS0yODE4NzhiODNkOGEiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=hmx5c-769MoWrCzgixDei-cYiLm0v9PwbEKhAF1tXpo=) Before my election to the State Senate in 2020, I led the Wisconsin Department of Agriculture Trade and Consumer Protection. In this role, I was responsible for advocating for farmers’ mental health, increased market opportunities for farmers, and rural prosperity through broadband, health care, and education. [If you agree that it’s time we had someone with the skills, experience, and values necessary to represent our district in Congress – rather than a far-right violent extremist – consider chipping in $20 to my campaign today.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/49415226/362048793/-822899351?refcode=E17852-20220818-BradStory-SL-CampaignNews-RegTemplate-NA-NA&amount=20&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzEvMS85MzIyMyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3MzQ3ZjFhMi0xOTFmLWVkMTEtYmQ2ZS0yODE4NzhiODNkOGEiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=hmx5c-769MoWrCzgixDei-cYiLm0v9PwbEKhAF1tXpo=) **Family is my rock, friend.** I met my wife Betty, a West Salem native, at a 4-H leadership luncheon in high school. Today, we are the proud parents of two college-aged children. In good times and challenging days, my family sustains me. **[Now, I’m running for WI-03.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/49415227/362048794/-822899351?refcode=E17852-20220818-BradStory-SL-CampaignNews-RegTemplate-NA-NA&amount=25&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzEvMS85MzIyMyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3MzQ3ZjFhMi0xOTFmLWVkMTEtYmQ2ZS0yODE4NzhiODNkOGEiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=hmx5c-769MoWrCzgixDei-cYiLm0v9PwbEKhAF1tXpo=)** **With the retirement of my friend and mentor, Rep. Ron Kind, our district is an ‘open seat’ this November.** [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/49415228/362048795/404025521?refcode=E17852-20220818-BradStory-graphic-CampaignNews-RegTemplate-NA-NA&amount=25&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzEvMS85MzIyMyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3MzQ3ZjFhMi0xOTFmLWVkMTEtYmQ2ZS0yODE4NzhiODNkOGEiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=hmx5c-769MoWrCzgixDei-cYiLm0v9PwbEKhAF1tXpo=) **I’m stepping up to continue representing the 3rd District in the way it deserves: with integrity, honesty, and always putting people first.** We do not need a representative who lives and promotes extremist views and distorted values in our district. From La Crosse, Eau Claire, and Stevens Point to the Wisconsin suburbs of Minneapolis-St. Paul, we are a district of hard workers who respect our community and share Wisconsin values. clean_body: My name is Brad Pfaff, and I’m honored to be the Democratic candidate for Wisconsin’s Third Congressional District. | = | Hi, friend. My name is Brad Pfaff, and I’m honored to be the Democratic candidate for Wisconsin’s Third Congressional District. = | = Wisconsin has always been my home. I grew up on my family’s dairy farm in northern La Crosse County, among the rolling hills, coulees, and valleys of “God’s Country.” As a farm boy, I learned the value of hard work, resilience, appreciation for the land, and respect for our community. The tried-and-true Wisconsin values my parents, neighbors, and teachers instilled remain with me today. Community service is one of those homegrown values and has informed my professional life. I earned my Bachelor of Arts degree in public and environmental administration from the University of Wisconsin — Green Bay and a Master of Public Administration from George Mason University. = This is me and Betty who would go on to be my wife! In 1997, I joined the congressional staff of Rep. Ron Kind, assisting him with agriculture and rural development issues for over 12 years. I’ve also been honored to work for Senator Herb Kohl and state Rep. Virgil Roberts. Deciding it was time to get into the arena, in 2007, I was elected to the La Cross County Board of Supervisors. In 2009, friend, I was privileged to serve the Obama Administration as the Wisconsin executive director for the Farm Service Agency at the U.S. Department of Agriculture and then, in 2015, as the USDA Deputy Administrator for Farm Programs. = Before my election to the State Senate in 2020, I led the Wisconsin Department of Agriculture Trade and Consumer Protection. In this role, I was responsible for advocating for farmers’ mental health, increased market opportunities for farmers, and rural prosperity through broadband, health care, and education. = Family is my rock, friend. I met my wife Betty, a West Salem native, at a 4-H leadership luncheon in high school. Today, we are the proud parents of two college-aged children. In good times and challenging days, my family sustains me. = With the retirement of my friend and mentor, Rep. | | Peter, **102 years ago today, the Nineteenth Amendment was ratified, guaranteeing women the right to vote in the Constitution.** As we celebrate the monumental achievement of equal voting rights between the sexes, let's remember that the fight for ballot access in this country is far, far from a relic of the history books. Voter suppression has been around for a long time, and it's taken many different forms over the years. Simply having the "right" to vote isn't much good if you can't actually use it. Poll taxes. Literacy tests. Purging of voting rolls. Limiting polling locations in certain precincts. Complicated requirements for obtaining an absentee ballot. Shifting "early vote" windows. **Same states have practically turned making it harder to vote into a dark art.** Fortunately, Oregon is a beacon of hope for how to protect and expand access to the ballot. We've had vote-by-mail since 2000. We cover the return postage for mailed ballots. Every mailbox is a polling place. And, in 2015, we passed our automatic voter registration law that has enfranchised hundreds of thousands of Oregonians who now receive a ballot in the mail and the opportunity to participate in the most fundamental part of our democracy. **Leading the floor debate in support of passing that bill remains one of the proudest moments from my time in the legislature.** So today, let's remember our history - the good and the bad - and recognize that while we have a lot of work ahead of us, we can win this fight to ensure free and fair elections across this country. clean_body: | | | | Peter, 102 years ago today, the Nineteenth Amendment was ratified, guaranteeing women the right to vote in the Constitution. As we celebrate the monumental achievement of equal voting rights between the sexes, let's remember that the fight for ballot access in this country is far, far from a relic of the history books. Voter suppression has been around for a long time, and it's taken many different forms over the years. Simply having the "right" to vote isn't much good if you can't actually use it. Poll taxes. Literacy tests. Purging of voting rolls. Limiting polling locations in certain precincts. Complicated requirements for obtaining an absentee ballot. Shifting "early vote" windows. Same states have practically turned making it harder to vote into a dark art. Fortunately, Oregon is a beacon of hope for how to protect and expand access to the ballot. We've had vote-by-mail since 2000. We cover the return postage for mailed ballots. Every mailbox is a polling place. And, in 2015, we passed our automatic voter registration law that has enfranchised hundreds of thousands of Oregonians who now receive a ballot in the mail and the opportunity to participate in the most fundamental part of our democracy. Leading the floor debate in support of passing that bill remains one of the proudest moments from my time in the legislature. So today, let's remember our history - the good and the bad - and recognize that while we have a lot of work ahead of us, we can win this fight to ensure free and fair elections across this country. But this grassroots movement has proved them wrong every step along the way, and now TX-23 is the most flippable seat in Texas.

| | Last week, on the House floor, GOP leader Kevin McCarthy asked us,_"Are Americans better off than they were two years ago?"_ **Yes, we are!** Two years ago – in the summer of 2020 – COVID was raging and vaccines were months away, over ten million Americans had lost their jobs, millions of Americans were struggling with food insecurity, and the stock market was plunging amid pandemic economic shocks. Since then, President Biden and the Democratic Congress are getting America back on track.
* Democrats passed the American Rescue Plan and delivered **500 million vaccine shots in arms** and sent relief checks to 160 million Americans.

* We passed the child tax credit, creating the biggest one-year **drop in childhood poverty** in American history.

* Way ahead of schedule, **American jobs have come roaring back** – and unemployment now stands at just 3.5%.

* Thanks to the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, we have invested $550 billion **repairing roads and bridges, updating the power grid, and providing broadband internet access.**

* **Computer chip manufacturing is coming back to America** , creating high-paying jobs and stronger national security.

* Harmed by toxic burn pits, **our veterans will get the health care they need.**

* We passed the **first gun safety legislation in 30 years** — with enhanced background checks, closing the "boyfriend loophole", and making gun trafficking a federal crime.

* Now, we are **taking on climate change** with huge investments in clean energy and electric vehicles.

* And for seniors on Medicare, **prescription drug costs will be capped at $2000 a year**.

clean_body: | | | | Last week, on the House floor, GOP leader Kevin McCarthy asked us,"Are Americans better off than they were two years ago?" Yes, we are! Two years ago – in the summer of 2020 – COVID was raging and vaccines were months away, over ten million Americans had lost their jobs, millions of Americans were struggling with food insecurity, and the stock market was plunging amid pandemic economic shocks. Since then, President Biden and the Democratic Congress are getting America back on track. Democrats passed the American Rescue Plan and delivered 500 million vaccine shots in arms and sent relief checks to 160 million Americans. We passed the child tax credit, creating the biggest one-year drop in childhood poverty in American history. Way ahead of schedule, American jobs have come roaring back – and unemployment now stands at just 3.5%. Thanks to the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, we have invested $550 billion repairing roads and bridges, updating the power grid, and providing broadband internet access. Computer chip manufacturing is coming back to America , creating high-paying jobs and stronger national security. Harmed by toxic burn pits, our veterans will get the health care they need. We passed the first gun safety legislation in 30 years — with enhanced background checks, closing the "boyfriend loophole", and making gun trafficking a federal crime. Now, we are taking on climate change with huge investments in clean energy and electric vehicles. And for seniors on Medicare, prescription drug costs will be capped at $2000 a year. There is a lot more to do, but over the last 18 months Democrats have been getting it done! **Peter Willis, all it takes is one surprise medical bill to send a patient into bankruptcy here in America.**
Right now, over 72 million people across the country are drowning in medical debt.
No one should die because they can’t afford medical treatment, and seeing a doctor shouldn’t put you into insurmountable debt— but that is the reality of our current healthcare system.
**I support the only policy that treats healthcare as a human right— Universal Healthcare with Medicare For All.**
I know these profit-hungry insurance companies won’t go down without a fight, Peter Willis. I’m ready to take them on, and thanks to the grassroots movement we are building, we’re one step closer to making Medicare for All a reality.

body:
Hello Folks,
It's back to school season! The summer has flown by. There are plenty of opportunities to donate school supplies and come together as a community for back to school season. I will be taking part in several charitable back-to-school events, and I hope you will too.
Here are some back to school events taking place in the 24th legislative district:
Glenarden Mayor Cashenna Cross in Partnership with Delegate Jazz Lewis; Back to School Bash Transitional Youth extravaganza happening
What: Back to school event with free backbacks, school supplies, lunch bags, music, games, & food.
When: Aug 27, 2022 9am-6pm
Where: Glenarden Community Center 8615 McLain Ave Glenarden Md 20706
Contact: maya@jazzlewis.com
Mission of Hope Charities' 6th Annual Community Day Event
What: Free backpack and school supply giveaway. Students from Kindergarten through High School will be given free backpacks filled with school supplies. Moon-bounce, Music, Games, Assurance Phone Services, CCI Mobile Dental Services, Impact Clinic – COVID Testing, & Horseback Riding.
Items needed, specifically for high school students: Backpacks, Water Bottles, Calculators, Mechanical Pencils, White-Out, Permanent Markers, Spiral Notebooks, Daily Planner, and Electronics.
When: 12 pm to 3 pm.
Where: Goodwin Park. 311 68th Place Seat Pleasant, MD 20743.
Contact: Gregory Torrence at gtorrence@molc-inc.org or 301-537-8196.
N’Style Hair Grooming Back To School Block Party.
What: Block party with food, live music, & giveaways.
When: Sunday, August 21st. 12 pm to 4 pm.
Where: Ritch Station Market Place. 1610 Ritch Station Court Capitol Heights, MD 20747.
Contact: Cynthia Miller at clmiller@leafyblossoms.com or (301) 335-1999.
Uplift Baptist Church, Back To School Fun Day.
What: Backpack and school supply distribution, food, games, music, & more.
When: Saturday, August 20th. 11 am to 3 pm.
Where: 7100 Martin Luther King Jr. Highway. Hyattesville, MD 20785.
Contact: admin@upliftbaptist.com
Town of Capital Heights: Back To School Community Day; with remarks from Delegate Jazz Lewis
What: School supply giveaway with vendors, food, music, face painting, a car show, & other family activities.
When: Saturday, August 20th. 12 pm to 4 pm.
Where: Corner of Capitol Heights Blvd. & Central Ave, extends to the Captiol Heights Metro Station.
Contact: Bverly Habada at (301) 332-1844
Dupont Village Neighborhood Watch Back to School, School Supply Event.
Where: 2405 Shadyside Ave. Suitland, MD 20746.
When: Sunday,, August 21st. 12 pm to 4 pm.
Let's support out students,
Jazz

P.O. Box 341854
Bethesda, MD 20827
United States

| [](http://trk.readactnews.-lJoOH9k78paoTlGFDEg)

| | Some highlights of this issue include:
* **“We Can’t Let Ukraine Lose” with Condoleezza Rice and Rachel Martin** – Hoover director Condoleezza Rice says Russia’s invasion is “disastrous for the liberal world order. It’s disastrous for Europe. It’s disastrous for all the values we hold dear.”
* **“Lands of the Lost” by Victor Davis Hanson** – Modern History teems with irredentism – a bloody march of messiahs and autocrats trying to “reclaim” lost lands. Where will Putin’s forces halt?
* **“Once Burned” by Kenneth C. Griffin and Niall Ferguson** – When Europe made itself dependent on Russian natural gas, it fueled Putin’s aggression and made itself vulnerable. New sources of energy, especially from the United States, can fix that.

**[Click here to get your free copy](http://trk.readactnews.-5d14pm9YBA) **of the 2022 Summer edition of the _Hoover Digest_ right now.

Peter, We’ve seen decent Republican leaders like Anthony Gonzalez, Adam Kinzinger, Mitt Romney, and Liz Cheney chose to stand up for America and defy Trump.
While this handful of Republicans did the right thing, other politicians have used Trump's assault on democracy to increase their own power. Max Miller is one of those politicians. He kissed up to President Trump as a White House aide, even [helping Trump plan January 6th](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/atcYNHk4Eh2YdGnwBh-YDPZfewv8ssItGGgKRecO6g94AOUpbVBIYmw5DvIns4d6gcOhWdbcXle2IhYg9FaFOEmtXMvKpHxVBTNqSWlqQO5guYsCQcUSu_qWTWqEgu884PVY6_nJm1N7As_Dm8kaK1GtQpps_7KaNBO8fBEJpFlzLW4mN2MMz_6_uzxXw8Pw4NBuYLFElzXA-0F6ifxrt5Dh8XV2lomM3I93sEWis_ebIiHG75j1WqCj5H52vXU7Ueg9UeT4A8Vg39-GC3BfTlmhb3ybfL7fJ4KHeZSXBdULBWjBtXzqY0gp0IWktRNySR1biJGT4fyrLwGOxf82ietfMG3G9ocu0gheFCZV_pfL437IyzhY1b2zjL1qRCoweUNOSuHZg4wVNiFOS5ApFw/3op/oGnqIOyCRfuS5Y_HIskuqQ/h0/Qd8Vakidxh_j5BlolPz24zWi6OIpexP896d9HRyGIpw). Then, he moved to our newly gerrymandered Republican district to run for Congress, and won the Republican nomination because he had Trump's support.

body:
hey, team, it's been a while.
Hi folks –
It's been a while since I checked in with you, and I wanted to have a quick chat.
I'm in between meetings with community leaders, but this couldn't wait. As you may have seen, my race against the GOP is tight.
The latest poll has me narrowly beating my opponent, but we can't afford to take any chances. My opponent is a Trumpian, alt-right, gun lobbyist-endorsed extremist with no policy experience whatsoever.
I understand the past few years have been tough to be engaged in politics. Seeing Trump win and then carry an insurrection to the doorstep of democracy was enough to make me question everything I knew about national security and American values.
But I got back up. I took those questions and I channeled them into a way that I could make a difference: by running for Congress.
Now, I need you to stand up with me. It's defeatist to say the fight for a Democratic majority is long gone. But, the truth is, we have a strong chance here and around the country now, and there are millions of Americans whose rights are at stake. We don't have the privilege of waiting for another chance.
**My mid-month fundraising deadline is here, and I need all the help I can get to cross the finish line ahead of my GOP opponent. Will you chip in $25 or whatever you can support my campaign and this fight?** You can donate here: [secure.actblue.com/donate/el-email](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/49420908/362071406/1579145984?refcode2=2ca0ff86-2c1f-ed11-bd6e-281878b83d8a&amount=25&refcode=220818_el_midmonth_l1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjQvMS85MzY4MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyY2EwZmY4Ni0yYzFmLWVkMTEtYmQ2ZS0yODE4NzhiODNkOGEiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=4O2BRCjciH70mq3j0P5xxmULHVqUDc812xYuGFUPBbw=)

body:
Senate Republicans just blocked a measure to cap the cost of insulin copays at $35 a month.
| | |
---
**Peter, Senate Republicans just blocked a measure to cap the cost of insulin copays at $35 a month. **It's just plain wrong that in 2022 Americans have to choose between paying for groceries and paying for lifesaving medication.
**As a nurse, but also just a person with compassion and empathy, I know how essential it is that we reduce the cost of insulin for the millions of American families who are struggling to afford this lifesaving medication.** During my time working in a local hospital, as a children's advocate, and on the campaign trail, I've heard so many stories about the pain these prices cause families. This is an urgent problem that American families are _counting_ on Washington to fix.
But right now, leaders in Congress care more about cashing huge checks from Big Pharma than fighting for the people they're supposed to serve. **Those partisan leaders don't seem to get that the point of healthcare isn't to make Big Pharma richer – it's to serve people and help them live healthier, more fulfilling lives.**
There's a lot that we have to do to fix our broken healthcare system, drive down costs, and ensure high quality care. Addressing all those issues won't happen overnight, but lowering the cost of insulin would have an immediate, massive impact for millions.
When I am in the Senate, you can count on me to make insulin and other lifesaving drugs more affordable. **But until we vote out the extremists who shot down this legislation and expand our Senate majority, Mitch McConnell and his cronies are going to keep on blocking it**. **[That's why I have to ask: Please, can I count on you to make a donation to flip Missouri blue, fix our broken healthcare system, and send a nurse's heart to the Senate? It's just plain wrong that in 2022 Americans have to choose between paying for groceries and paying for lifesaving medication. As a nurse, but also just a person with compassion and empathy, I know how essential it is that we reduce the cost of insulin for the millions of American families who are struggling to afford this lifesaving medication. During my time working in a local hospital, as a children's advocate, and on the campaign trail, I've heard so many stories about the pain these prices cause families. This is an urgent problem that American families are counting on Washington to fix. But right now, leaders in Congress care more about cashing huge checks from Big Pharma than fighting for the people they're supposed to serve. Those partisan leaders don't seem to get that the point of healthcare isn't to make Big Pharma richer – it's to serve people and help them live healthier, more fulfilling lives. There's a lot that we have to do to fix our broken healthcare system, drive down costs, and ensure high quality care. Addressing all those issues won't happen overnight, but lowering the cost of insulin would have an immediate, massive impact for millions. When I am in the Senate, you can count on me to make insulin and other lifesaving drugs more affordable. But until we vote out the extremists who shot down this legislation and expand our Senate majority, Mitch McConnell and his cronies are going to keep on blocking it. = If you've saved payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | | | = | | = | | = | | = Together, we can send the first nurse to the U.S. Senate and win a better, healthier future for all of us. Friend, I'm reaching out today to talk about what makes Florida so different. It comes down to one word: decency.
Like you, I've been shocked and dismayed by how vulgar and mean-spirited our politics have become. I was devastated to learn of the Supreme Court's decision to overturn Roe v. Wade.
Leaders should work to unite us around policies that will help everyone, not divide and distract us. And I know from experience that it starts at the top.
Every day, I strive to live according to The Golden Rule: "Do unto others as you would have them do unto you."
Our current Governor don't seem to share those same values.
Floridians want leaders who lead with kindness, selflessness, and above all else: decency. ★ We support common-sense gun reform to put an end to the terrible mass shooting.
★ We support women’s autonomy over their own bodies.
★ And we overwhelmingly support following the science to guide us out of the COVID-19 pandemic instead of spreading anti-vaccine conspiracy theories.
Unfortunately, Governor DeSantis doesn't agree with the vast majority of Floridians on these issues. His radical agenda is extreme and out of line with Florida values.
We can stop his dangerous agenda — but only if we’re willing to stand up and do our part.
DeSantis may not care about decency, but I believe Floridians still do. If you agree, I hope you’ll take a stand for what you believe in. We all have to do our part to ensure that decency will trump divisiveness.

clean_body: | | | | = Friend, I'm reaching out today to talk about what makes Florida so different. It comes down to one word: decency. Like you, I've been shocked and dismayed by how vulgar and mean-spirited our politics have become. I was devastated to learn of the Supreme Court's decision to overturn Roe v. Wade. Leaders should work to unite us around policies that will help everyone, not divide and distract us. And I know from experience that it starts at the top. Every day, I strive to live according to The Golden Rule: "Do unto others as you would have them do unto you." Our current Governor don't seem to share those same values. Floridians want leaders who lead with kindness, selflessness, and above all else: decency. = = The truth is, self-serving politicians try to divide us so that we don't realize how much we actually agree on. But after talking to people across the state, I can promise you — Floridians agree on a lot. ★ We support common-sense gun reform to put an end to the terrible mass shooting. ★ We support women’s autonomy over their own bodies. ★ And we overwhelmingly support following the science to guide us out of the COVID-19 pandemic instead of spreading anti-vaccine conspiracy theories. Unfortunately, Governor DeSantis doesn't agree with the vast majority of Floridians on these issues. His radical agenda is extreme and out of line with Florida values. We can stop his dangerous agenda — but only if we’re willing to stand up and do our part. DeSantis may not care about decency, but I believe Floridians still do. name: Hill Harper @ Three Star
subject: We have our keynote speaker — Hill Harper!
body:
Peter,

We are thrilled to announce that our keynote speaker for this year's Three Star Dinner will be award winning actor, best selling author, and founder/CEO of The Black Wall Street, Hill Harper. Harper starred on the TV drama CSI: NY and on The Good Doctor, in addition to many other roles. He is the author of four New York Times best-sellers and haas earned seven NAACP Image Awards for his writing and acting. Harper is also the founder of the Manifest Your Destiny Foundation, dedicated to empowering underserved youth through mentorship, scholarship, and grant programs.

We are also excited to have our Democratic candidate for Governor, Dr. Jason Martin, join to share his vision, along with Mayor Lee Harris of Shelby County and Mayor John Cooper of Nashville.

Purchase your tickets and sponsorships now:

Tickets and Sponsorships [https://www.tndp.org/threestar/]
https://www.tndp.org/threestar/ [https://www.tndp.org/threestar/]

We couldn't be more excited to host the 2022 Three Star Dinner, and we hope you join us for the biggest celebration of the year with fellow Democrats.

See you on August 27th,

Hendrell Remus

name: Chrissy
subject: Do you agree with SCOTUS’ decision to overturn Roe v. Wade?
body:
| | |
---
Derek, I know it has been a heart-rending few months since the Supreme Court overturned Roe v. Wade in June.
Not only has the right to abortion been lost at the federal level, but many anti-abortion lawmakers – including too many of my Pennsylvania colleagues – have rushed to implement statewide abortion bans that put women at risk.
We won’t stand for it – but look at Kansas. Years ago, it was the epicenter of some of the most extreme anti-abortion activities in the country. Yet in a referendum vote the other week, abortion rights supporters celebrated a resounding victory. While we know our fight doesn't start and end at the polls – voting remains one of the most powerful tools for all of us to hold politicians accountable and influence policy.
That's why as a mom, teacher, and congresswoman, I have been fighting relentlessly for women, making sure they have equity and the fundamental right to make their own health decisions. I know it's been a long summer in the fight for reproductive freedom, but we need to continue to fight back and build majorities that will codify Roe v. Wade once and for all.
**Abortion access is essential and lifesaving – and I will never stop fighting for it. I need to know that you’re with me:**
| | **Do you agree that we need to codify Roe v. Wade?**

clean_body: | | | Derek, I know it has been a heart-rending few months since the Supreme Court overturned Roe v. Wade in June. Not only has the right to abortion been lost at the federal level, but many anti-abortion lawmakers – including too many of my Pennsylvania colleagues – have rushed to implement statewide abortion bans that put women at risk. We won’t stand for it – but look at Kansas. Years ago, it was the epicenter of some of the most extreme anti-abortion activities in the country. Yet in a referendum vote the other week, abortion rights supporters celebrated a resounding victory. While we know our fight doesn't start and end at the polls – voting remains one of the most powerful tools for all of us to hold politicians accountable and influence policy. That's why as a mom, teacher, and congresswoman, I have been fighting relentlessly for women, making sure they have equity and the fundamental right to make their own health decisions. I know it's been a long summer in the fight for reproductive freedom, but we need to continue to fight back and build majorities that will codify Roe v. Wade once and for all. body:
Largest Retirement Tax Cut for Veterans in VA HistoryDear friends, I just wanted to take a moment and reach out to all of you to make sure you know what exactly my bill, SB528, will actually do for our flourishing community of veterans in Virgi
| | | |
---
| Largest Retirement Tax Cut for Veterans in VA History
---
| Dear friends, I just wanted to take a moment and reach out to all of you to make sure you know what exactly my bill, SB528, will actually do for our flourishing community of veterans in Virginia. I know the title of this email seems a little far-fetched, but it's true. We have never, in the Commonwealth of Virginia, offered tax exemptions on military retiree pay before. This bill will not only encourage our service members to stay here in Virginia when they retire, rather than going to another state for their tax exemptions, but will also put a lot of money right back into our economy. Most service members start a second job or even open up a small business after retirement, and bring highly valuable skills learned in the military to the civilian work force. Let's get into the nitty gritty of what my bill actually does: If you are are 55 or older and receive any of the following benefits, then you are eligible for the tax deduction:-Retirement income for service in the Armed Forces-Military benefits paid out to the surviving spouse of a service member-Benefits paid out under the DOD's Survivor Benefits Program-"Certain military benefits" as defined in the IRS Code (Any allowance or in-kind benefit, not including personal use of a vehicle, that is received by a service member or dependent) So if you receive any of the above benefits, and are 55 or older as mentioned, here are the individual income tax subtractions you can claim: -Up to $10,000 for FY2022-Up to $20,000 for FY2023-Up to $30,000 for FY2024-Up to $40,000 for FY2025, and beyond This much-needed tax cut for our veterans will show our service members that our Commonwealth values them and respects all that they have given to our country. Considering that Virginia has a massive population of active duty service members and a veteran population of nearly 700 thousand, this will greatly affect a multitude of families right here at home. With the weight of these trying times on all Americans' shoulders, I hope that this will have a positive effect on folks here in our Commonwealth, and will set an example for states who have not yet enacted similar legislation. As always, it is an honor and a privilege to be your representative in Richmond, and I will continue fighting for the freedoms and values that we all share and enjoy. Yours in Service, Senator Bryce E. Reeves

subject: Reminder: I want to set the record straight
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY DIEHL FOR MASSACHUSETTS
body:
| | | |
---
| Friends,
I want to set the record straight, once and for all.
First, I did not get into this race to help the Boston Globe -- one of the nation's most liberal newspapers -- sell its left-wing propaganda to readers.
Let's face it. The Globe never has anything positive to say about Republicans, including me. I've been the bane of their editorials for years, simply because I have the courage to stand up and express views that don't fit their liberal talking points.
So earlier today I publicly rejected an invitation from their editorial board to "interview" for the Globe's endorsement. Their editorial page is essentially just a bulletin board for left-wing progressive talking points and utopian daydreams, and I'm not playing into it.
---
| | [Read Geoff's Full Statement About the Globe](https://r20.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001kr_Lc4kAVgCQAQrHiSX5OKodBwFE-GDOBuJ7oY33hbuHQf7Ht2nH5Wfevwz4IbXREqQyIBH_N57Iux_1Q-DAflPn4ndA5ca_8IhW3GwehkqujXbSp47owuQ9mfrlYe_Im4pkw3fLeHomCF1aa0SH2bWE4pnSemi6h2PI6fisav1RG_PUeshm2RJmhqThySGJSZ_NVpyiBAT92U7zpUJ2W8cOy2fkEHamc7fIZjao-0c=&c=l9V-vXl8tXmyNtqIM7b0EUo60WEfROOJrg3i3orfkQZk1zP9p5pXhg==&ch=oYV4Ux_usGINmB8hk2442HPUHOvXBtWRfsH4lNTY5HctQ_0pYVRb9A==)
---
| Second, I did not get into this race to help my opponent, who has no record because he's never run for public office, raise his political profile with free air time.
I challenged my opponent to two debates as soon as we both qualified for the ballot. He accepted one invitation, and we debated -- for a full hour, live on The Howie Carr Show, in front of studio guests and with a prime drive-time audience listening.
My opponent failed to accept a second debate, on the Jeff Kuhner Show. I'm not one to renege on my promises, so I kept the scheduled appearance and took questions from Jeff Kuhner and his listeners live, on-air for more than an hour. I was happy to do it and we got a great response. You can hear the whole thing here:
---
| | [Listen to Geoff Diehl on The Kuhner Report](https://r20.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001kr_Lc4kAVgCQAQrHiSX5OKodBwFE-GDOBuJ7oY33hbuHQf7Ht2nH5Wfevwz4IbXRLdfuOmB5T5KEuzMjD8Ua3RibEa-oo3361bmr8hiHKNbJt0Ya0LlczA3sAX_2IslwEVgnxnj2Jh664DzYQWoz9F6uFuCaObE5tf15Ja-tGiUbHEPiybWrytZa5zIkp2iB3mn1t-FFUZFX8Dnb6MzVPb6V78VyHUcr65O5zHxV2aXeAwvaNVBcedIIXktXZYljjCCba3PyDi5SwFKT_TiC27TvMN2r-cRJ&c=l9V-vXl8tXmyNtqIM7b0EUo60WEfROOJrg3i3orfkQZk1zP9p5pXhg==&ch=oYV4Ux_usGINmB8hk2442HPUHOvXBtWRfsH4lNTY5HctQ_0pYVRb9A==)
---
| I think my opponent now realizes his bad tactical error because he keeps calling for more and more pre-primary debates -- ten in all! (Lincoln and Douglas, who made political debates famous, only needed seven debates to resolve the presidency!)
Look, my opponent had a full hour to say whatever he wanted to, and he declined another hour of debate to further state his case. If he now feels he missed his shot, that's not up to me to fix, and it doesn't do the voters any service to fight about it.
I am running for exactly one reason: to protect and enhance your freedom and prosperity. I consider anything that doesn't further that cause to be a distraction and a waste of your time. I'm not pandering to the Globe or my opponent.
This race isn't about newspaper endorsements, debates, or slick television ads. It's about who is going to protect your freedom, cut taxes, stand up against mandates, educate your kids, and fix our broken transportation systems. I sincerely believe my experience in the public and private sectors, together with my lengthy conservative track record, uniquely qualifies me for the job. I'm the most electable candidate in this race. I've won 5 races in a row. My opponent has 0 wins.
The latest polling has us leading this race three-to-one. Leah Allen and I won the Republican Convention's endorsement two-to-one. Now, I'm working hard to bring our message to you, one-on-one. I don't need a filter or a moderator to help me out.
I'm not giving in, and I'm not backing down. Leah Allen and I are here to fight for you, the People of Massachusetts.
That's the real story, straight from me. Don't accept spin from anyone to the contrary. Leah and I are here to win this race and to lead Massachusetts forward in 2023.
In victory,
---

A Republican-appointed judge just reinstated North Carolina’s 20-week abortion ban. Next up? A total abortion ban in our state.
#

A Republican-appointed judge just reinstated North Carolina’s 20-week abortion ban. Next up? A total abortion ban in our state.
North Carolina is one of the only southern states with access to abortion, but our rights are still under attack by politicians like my opponent Congressman Ted Budd.
This was only possible because of the Dobbs decision overturning _Roe v. Wade_ , and if given the chance in the U.S. Senate, my opponent will absolutely try to pass a nationwide ban without exceptions.
We will not back down as out-of-step politicians like Congressman Budd work to take away our constitutional freedoms. Period. And I will not hesitate to cast the decisive vote to secure this freedom in the U.S. Senate. Period.
We cannot allow politicians to roll back our rights any further. This is why we must win this race and expand our majority.

name: Peter Welch
subject: College tuition has increased by 2000% since I was in school
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY WELCH FOR VERMONT
body:
Millions face a crushing debt, just for pursuing a higher education

# [](https://act.welchforvermont.com/go/144?t=2&akid=821%2E61531%2Eqo0KQa)
Hello,
To say higher education costs have gone up is the understatement of the century. From 1970 (around when I graduated college) to 2020, tuition costs have exploded by more than _**2,000 percent**_. It’s no wonder millions of students and their families need to rely on student loans.
What was once a gateway to the middle-class has become a crushing financial burden on those trying to achieve the American Dream of a better life. Instead of supporting students, we’re punishing them with a lifetime of debt for simply pursuing a higher education.
That’s why I’m fighting for a comprehensive approach to student debt—one I’ll continue to fight for in the Senate:
1. **Make college affordable:** I cosponsored the Debt Free College Act to incentivize states to offer debt free college by unlocking matching federal funds.
2. **Expand access to community college and public colleges:** The College for All Act, which I also cosponsored, would waive tuition and fees for every community college student and qualifying students at public colleges and universities.
3. **Reduce the burden of student loans:** This is the one I need your help with. I’ve signed a letter to President Biden, calling on him to cancel up to $50,000 of each borrower’s federal student loan debt.

I’ve fought for this issue for a long time because Vermonters bear a disproportionate burden of student debt—facing an average debt of $31k, which is even higher than the $28k national average. Vermont has some of the best colleges in the country—it’s only fair that people are able to afford them.
No one should be forced into crushing debt just to pay for college. If you agree we need real action to lower costs and reduce student debt, sign your name under mine on this letter to President Biden.
[ADD YOUR NAME ](https://act.welchforvermont.com/signup/em-cancel-student-loan-debt-biden/?source=em_20220818_p_p_studentdebt&t=5&t=6&akid=821%2E61531%2Eqo0KQa)
---
Thanks for being in this fight,
Peter

In his time in Congress, Peter is widely recognized as a progressive leader and a skillful legislator who chooses governing over gridlock. That’s clear in his record: Peter is an original cosponsor of the Green New Deal and is a leading advocate for lowering the cost of prescription drugs, providing affordable childcare, expanding access to broadband in rural America, and protecting our imperiled democracy.

clean_body: | | | Dear Peter, OLCV is thrilled to continue our set of summer youth engagement events, “This is How We Win: Climate Organizing 100 Series” with our second workshop installment: Winning Elections 101! Though this event is geared towards youth with a budding interest in politics and climate organizing, anybody passionate about environmental activism is welcome to sign up. This entry-level interactive seminar will broadly address the different levels of work that go into winning elections, and how people can get involved to contribute towards successful climate campaigns. Led by OLCV’s organizing team and youth interns, “Winning Elections 101” is sure to be an exciting and informative time. This event will be held on Wednesday, August 31st from 5:30-6:45 PM via Zoom, allowing participants to join us from all over Oregon. As the second workshop in our climate organizing series, attendees can turn what they’ve learned into action during our third and final event: an in-person “Canvassing 101” course in Portland where we’ll be spreading the word about Tina Kotek’s candidacy for governor as a true climate champion. Keep your eyes peeled for more information on that next month and With election season right around the corner this November, learning about our political process and what can be done to enact positive change through it is more important than ever. We’re here to help by making complicated political processes easy to understand, and we look forward to having you. Thank you, I hope to see you there! subject: 102 years of women’s voting rights—and the need to do even better
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Friends of Lashrecse Aird
body:
https://www.lashrecseaird.com [https://www.lashrecseaird.com]
Friends,
On August 18 we celebrate the 102 year anniversary of the ratification of the 19th Amendment—the Amendment that finally gave women the right to vote. But how many people know the harsh truth that the 19th Amendment didn’t give all women the right to vote? I’ll explain in a moment.
Join our Team [https://www.lashrecseaird.com/volunteer]
First, consider that only wealthy white land owning men could vote from our nation’s founding in 1776 until the 19th Amendment’s ratification in 1920. Meaning, for nearly 60% of our nation’s existence, women, Black people, Native Americans, or any person of color was excluded from the American promise of equal justice.
Donate [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/lashrecse]
And while the 19th Amendment was a crucial step in the right direction, we cannot forget who it left behind. Asian women were denied equal voting rights until 1952, Native women were denied equal voting rights until 1962, Black women were denied equal voting rights until 1965, and Latina women were denied equal voting rights until 1975 when accessible language ballots were finally enforced.
Sign up [https://www.lashrecseaird.com/volunteer]
Today, voting rights are still under attack and we must continue to defend them . I was proud as Delegate to vote for the Voting Rights Act of Virginia [https://lis.virginia.gov/cgi-bin/legp604.exe?ses=212&typ=bil&val=HB1890] to ensure every Virginian has free, fair, and easy access to the ballot box. I’m running for Virginia Senate because for too long, our underrepresented communities have been denied the promise of equal justice in America. It’s time to change the status quo, and fulfill the promise of justice for all.
Donate, volunteer, sign up for our email list. Join our campaign for true justice. Let’s get to work!
Sincerely,
Lashrecse

subject: We Keep Challenging the Left….
body:
You are one of our loyal supporters, so you know how Judicial Watch is working hard every day to fight for the rule of law and against public corruption and unlawful government secrecy

| |

| Dear Fellow American,

Thanks to support from hundreds of thousands of patriotic Americans, Judicial Watch is fighting harder today, and breaking new ground, on a number of very important policy fronts.
And we need your help today to keep the pressure on!
| [Contribute](https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=59835&L=17813&F=H&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9uYXRlL3RoYW5rLXlvdS0xMzUvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249TWF5JnV0bV90ZXJtPU5vbi1Eb25vcnM=)
---

_In just the past three weeks_ :

* On the heels of our successful lawsuit that forced the release of documents from the **S. Military Academy at West Point** that proved cadets are being indoctrinated in **Critical Race Theory** propaganda, we filed a Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) lawsuit against the U.S. Defense Department seeking similar records related to CRT propaganda at the **U.S. Naval Academy** ;

* And we filed two "friends of the court" briefs with our friends at the Allied Educational Foundation...the first supporting **a legal challenge to race-based****admissions programs at Harvard and the University of North Carolina** , and the other a challenge to a **race-based admissions policy** at a nationally-known public high school in the Washington, DC, suburb of Fairfax County, Virginia.

* And we continue to pursue our lawsuits against **Colorado** , **Illinois, New York** and **Pennsylvania** over their failure to follow federal law and clean their voter rolls between elections.

There's no summer break when it comes to fighting for the rule of law!

We aim to leave no stone unturned in our investigations. We will meet every court deadline; review every government document released to us; and take sworn depositions from key witnesses and persons of interest...

In short, _we are applying maximum pressure and staying firmly on track with all of our important work_.

So I must ask you an important question...[will you support us with a special tax-deductible contribution today?](https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=59835&L=17813&F=H&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9uYXRlL3RoYW5rLXlvdS0xMzUvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249TWF5JnV0bV90ZXJtPU5vbi1Eb25vcnM=)

**Thanks to support from our members, your _Judicial Watch is the largest_** **_and most effective government watchdog organization in America_.**

_We are proudly conservative_. _But Judicial Watch is completely nonpartisan_. _We do not endorse or oppose candidates for public office_. In all that we do, our commitment is to uphold the rule of law.

In today's environment that means we are _especially_ committed to doing our part in the courts to see that our elections are honest, open and fair.

And Judicial Watch is _still_ "the only game in town" exposing and stopping the chronic corruption and unlawful secrecy of out-of-control federal agencies... _like the_ _politicized Biden Justice Department and FBI that raided Mar-a-Lago_!

Judicial Watch's _independent investigations and lawsuits continue to be the way to challenge the "swamp" culture of Washington, DC_!

**This is so important today because I believe we are at a point where government corruption and unlawful government secrecy continue as a fundamental threat to our nation.**

By giving your support to Judicial Watch, you will be joining the fight _for_ the rule of law and _against_ public corruption. [I urge you to join with us and help us save our Republic.](https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=59835&L=17813&F=H&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9uYXRlL3RoYW5rLXlvdS0xMzUvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249TWF5JnV0bV90ZXJtPU5vbi1Eb25vcnM=)

[That is why I hope you can help today with an especially generous gift.](https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=59835&L=17813&F=H&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9uYXRlL3RoYW5rLXlvdS0xMzUvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249TWF5JnV0bV90ZXJtPU5vbi1Eb25vcnM=)

Peter, last school year we saw the highest number of school shootings on record.
After the shooting at Robb Elementary, schools in Uvalde got more safety officers. But what about every other school in Texas?

body:

| Friends,
I would like to congratulate my spectacular running mate, Leah Allen, for her outstanding performance that won this morning's debate for Lieutenant Governor.
Leah wasn't afraid to talk about the tough issues, the subjects that are really affecting Massachusetts families and businesses these days. She spoke eloquently about her work as a Registered Nurse during COVID, and losing her job because she refused to get vaccinated. She spoke about how the Legislature is putting its summer vacation plans ahead of the interests of Massachusetts residents, who could really use a tax break. She talked about the importance of personal freedoms and how we need to not only respect individual rights in the Executive and Legislative branches, but also how we need judges who will enforce the law from the bench.
You can watch a video of Leah's debate here:
---
[](https://r20.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001wQEtFm9W_NDvvM4_FGS0FIkdyCqwEDPQi9NmbFC_MLAOQS3Kayp28_ahQIfDt5ZMjUVdcBTdLTMgwyA9hEWTdv9oZr71aK-M0PloDrUsJJCu2OBGIb6M-MZBTpkCcjQy1edKYWS4x-w7EZnlrSpvbg==&c=Ntv7cpGr56t0UDPNyO2HSYO0Jp1QYO58lsV5cwNy24xZJFx2uhYNhw==&ch=yubdg6LhvoB5hT69eYKPZ6tlXSUXo-z1wiJoyKjHdajR4OxuEbPxlA==)

| I can't wait for Leah Allen to be our next Lieutenant Governor and to work together with her as a team to lead our state forward.
Unfortunately, our opponents in this race are trying to distract attention away from these issues. Leah and I aren't going to let them. There is too much at stake in this race. You, your freedom, and your prosperity are all at stake. Leah and I are singularly focused on making our state a better place to live and work, based on the conservative principles we've both proudly been defending for more than a decade. Our lengthy track record as stalwart conservatives has earned us the endorsement of prominent national Republicans like President Donald Trump and Governor Kristi Noem. It also earned us both convincing wins at the MassGOP Convention in May.
I remain confident voters will agree and support both of us at the Republican primary on September 6.
As always, Leah and I really appreciate your support. Thank you.

> PRESS RELEASE
Vikram for N.H. Announces Primary Campaign Steering Committee

---
CONCORD, NH - August 18, 2022 - Vikram Mansharamani today announced the formation of a diverse campaign steering committee that will advise him and the campaign on reaching its strategic goals. The steering committee features a prominent cadre of endorsers including:
-Augusta Petrone (Longtime Republican statewide donor and activist) -Jeremy Hitchcock (New Hampshire businessman; founder of Dyn) -Andy McLane (New Hampshire investor) -Geoff Krill (Longtime Lincoln Area resident and adaptive sports activist) -Rep. Josh Whitehouse (former N.H. State Representative and Trump Campaign/Administration Official)
A legend in New Hampshire politics, Dublin's Augusta Petrone, said of Vikram:
"I believe we have (by-and-large) a superb bench running for U.S. Senate from New Hampshire. However, Vikram Mansharamani is a quality candidate, with wide foreign relations experience (like working in the U.S. Embassy in Beijing and travelling for work in dozens of countries)--a valuable background for a U.S. Senator's work."
Another steering committee member, Lincoln's Geoff Krill has known Vikram for years as a neighbor in his hometown of Lincoln.
Geoff asserts: "I've known Vikram as a community activist and someone who takes real pride in his community. Through his efforts on behalf of the disabled sports community, for which I'm a strong advocate, Vikram has always been someone that achieves better outcomes on anything that he puts his mind to. He will take that same tactic to Washington for the people of New Hampshire."
Over the next few weeks, more New Hampshire endorsers will be announced to the steering committee. The group will focus squarely on grassroots and fundraising objectives for a Senate campaign that will win the primary on September 13th and take on Maggie Hassan this fall.

State Representative and Trump Campaign/Administration Official) A legend in New Hampshire politics, Dublin's Augusta Petrone, said of Vikram: "I believe we have (by-and-large) a superb bench running for U.S. Senate from New Hampshire. However, Vikram Mansharamani is a quality candidate, with wide foreign relations experience (like working in the U.S. Embassy in Beijing and travelling for work in dozens of countries)--a valuable background for a U.S. Senator's work." Another steering committee member, Lincoln's Geoff Krill has known Vikram for years as a neighbor in his hometown of Lincoln. Geoff asserts: "I've known Vikram as a community activist and someone who takes real pride in his community. Through his efforts on behalf of the disabled sports community, for which I'm a strong advocate, Vikram has always been someone that achieves better outcomes on anything that he puts his mind to. He will take that same tactic to Washington for the people of New Hampshire." Over the next few weeks, more New Hampshire endorsers will be announced to the steering committee. The group will focus squarely on grassroots and fundraising objectives for a Senate campaign that will win the primary on September 13th and take on Maggie Hassan this fall. | ### | | == | | | == == == | | | | | | | Vikram for NH | P.O. Fellow Conservative,

**The same Democrat party that just authorized the unprecedented FBI raid of President Trump’s home over “documents” just voted to give the IRS enough of your hard-earned money to hire 87,000 new IRS agents to come after the rest of us**.

**In what world is 87,000 new IRS agents a priority for our country?**

Sure, the Democrats claim they are just trying to squeeze every possible penny they can out of the American people to fund Biden’s dangerous agenda.**But I think there is much, much more to this power grab.**

**Ask yourself this:** __Why not use that same $80 billion to hire 87,000 new border patrol agents instead? Better yet, why not let people keep their own hard-earned money for themselves and their families?__

**Yes, showering the IRS with funds is about Democrats wanting more of our hard-earned money.** But to me, it’s just as much about the fundamental choice that Americans have faced since our founding. At the turn of the 20th century, my great-grandmother, Teresa, immigrated to the United States and put down roots in a small Italian neighborhood in Cleveland, Ohio. She had five daughters, including my grandmother, Pearl.
Back then, things were very different. Many people believed that women should rarely leave the house, and that politics was strictly men's business. But because of the courage, sacrifice, and protests of the women who came before me, I and millions of other women have the ability to make our voices heard.
Teresa was the first woman in my family to ever cast a ballot. Even as voting rights are still under attack in America, my great-grandmother’s courage has always inspired me to stand up for the right to vote.
We'll often face pushback while fighting for the things we believe in – as I’m sure you know, there will always be loud opponents of equality. But even as fundamental rights like the right to choose are being threatened here in Michigan and across the country, my grandmother’s bravery will always encourage me to keep up the fight.
[I’m the first and only woman to represent MI-11, and that’s an honor I’ll never forget. Did you know Jerry Moran’s PAC donated $50,000 to the campaign behind the anti-abortion measure? But that’s not all: Moran ran his own ads trying to convince people to vote yes on the measure and overturn abortion access here in Kansas — it’s clear he is out of touch with voters.
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/49428959/362103394/-963777892?amount=10&source=MH_EM_FR_3MO_220818_1_3&refcode2=&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzEvMS85MzM1NyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2ZTIwZTY3Ni00NzFmLWVkMTEtYmQ2ZS0yODE4NzhiODNkOGEiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=PaAs-e9_jbUCcyYe17_Q_mMbPYLLSipzrnFMKNd_v9M=)

Good Evening!

Due to the record closeness of our primary race, we have taken the advice and opportunity to file for a recount. I have been in contact with the county clerks, and the recount will be starting at 9:00 AM on Saturday in all six counties of the 2nd District. [Press Release](https://r20.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001DyLMQoXchwpU4Tgz6fRAzyzIGaEeLYl2pZ4Kl1ZqRzVWE28Tk5HZXl8b2PP-jqRuqqyr0-MrzFW23reNTgntF5hoe3qiexg22HUN8la7bbfMFINdRk_UXDlZE4EWp1JEtRyM7C3RnKfinsNt6mG9zeAqoqY0NxP4Vppl6HkD6TPKNm8Wg9KsgOBEjqZxuh-7yetcGvhoP6RammPgxxVw53bw9jsom2iLGNpMVDVEFh0-XeArQaH9kQ==&c=gE7IGs1_-6Dsk6Mp7jbfmMvWkGDRLibKvQ8d-INyJKhQ1F4n8PY9Jw==&ch=fuulWELAH95gCiLSf6Z91HoGVU2YPIyXGj6XO3EBUxFvXaZUfKXmxg==)

We will be hosting a training for those interested in getting involved in the election process on Friday evening. This training will be held in person in the 2nd Floor conference room at my office building, 437 S Yellowstone Dr., Madison, WI, and there will be a zoom link available as well. (Time(s) to be announced)

body:
**Friend, we need your help!** As the most important election of our lives is quickly approaching, we need to strengthen our grassroots army. This is a fight we cannot afford to lose, and we will only do it with your help. [****](https://act.wisgop.org/r?u=sxV_uZjhTYiS0NkYk0dD0eXv_5DaexUSZI9PlfXgIO8&e=d00ac07d22940c0f36f888b7fa3c8df2&utm_source=wisgop&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=help_wanted_v1&n=1) Picture this: it’s 2023. Ron Johnson is standing up for us in Washington, Tim Michels is fighting for our great state, and the Republicans elected all the way down the ballot are fixing our economy, supporting law enforcement, and securing our elections.
